pageProps.review: A guide on how to generate a product dependency graph in the AOSP build system using the m product-graph command, and convert it to PDF or SVG using the dot command.
pageProps.description: How to generate and visualize the AOSP product dependency graph using m product-graph and the dot command.
pageProps.content:
## Visualizing AOSP Product Dependency Graph
In the AOSP build system, you can generate a product dependency graph using the <mark>m product-graph</mark> command.  
It is useful for quickly understanding which products depend on which modules.
### 1. Generate the Dependency Graph
Initialize the build environment from the AOSP root directory, then run the following command.
```sh
{
    "title": "Generate product dependency graph"
}
---
$ source build/envsetup.sh
$ lunch <your_target>
//[!code highlight]
$ m product-graph
...
out/product-graph.dot
```
Once the command completes, the <mark>out/product-graph.dot</mark> file will be generated.
### 2. Convert to PDF or SVG using dot
The generated `.dot` file can be converted to various formats such as PDF or SVG using the `dot` command from <mark>Graphviz</mark>.
```sh
{
    "title": "Convert .dot to PDF or SVG"
}
---
# Convert to PDF
$ dot -Tpdf out/product-graph.dot -o product-graph.pdf

# Convert to SVG
$ dot -Tsvg out/product-graph.dot -o product-graph.svg
```
If the `dot` command is not available, install it as follows.
```sh
{
    "title": "Install Graphviz"
}
---
$ sudo apt-get install graphviz
```
Since SVG is a vector format, it remains crisp when opened in a browser or zoomed in, making it especially useful for large graphs.
